stories.title: Barber offers free back-to-school haircuts
stories.summary: A barber is offering free back-to-school haircuts, stationery and school essentials to help families facing rising costs. Sid Gumbrell, who runs Clean Cuts Barber Shop, in Guildford in Surrey, is hosting the event from 09:00 BST to 17:00 on Sunday. Children will also be able to pick up free stationery, pencil cases and water bottles. "To be honest, I know the struggles with the cost of things at the moment," Mr Gumbrell said. "School uniforms, shoes, haircuts, etc, it all adds up and if we can just help take one cost away it's a massive deal for us." He said the event was aimed at bringing children together while helping families with the cost of living. The day is being supported by Tesco and Krispy Kreme, which have donated towards the event. stories.title: Centenarian athlete grabs 2 golds at Daegu WMAC
stories.summary: DAEGU, Aug. 29 (Yonhap) -- Sawang Janpram, the oldest competitor taking part in ...
article_sentences: Sawang Janpram, the oldest competitor taking part in the World Masters Athletics Championships (WMAC) under way in the southern South Korean city of Daegu, won another gold medal Saturday, grabbing two golds at the event.
The Thai athlete, 106, won the gold medal in the men's 400-gram javelin throw for competitors aged 100 and older.
He threw 10.04 meters on his first attempt.
The win comes just two days after he won a gold in the 1-kilogram discus throw for competitors aged 100 and older by throwing 7.59 m, setting an amateur world record in the category.
Following the win Saturday, Janpram shortly said he is satisfied with his performance and is happy.
The Thai athlete and his daughter and coach Siripan, 74, are among the more than 11,000 participants from 106 countries taking part in WMAC Daegu.
WMAC Daegu runs through Thursday next week across 34 categories in the areas of track, field and road racing.
